item: A damaged database file is noticed, named and contained per file (E1)
key_paths: src/database/damage.py; src/database/session.py; src/versioned/store.py; src/scheduler/storage_guard.py; src/scheduler/runner.py; src/wiki/runner.py; src/api/scheduler.py; tests/test_database_damage.py; src/api/system.py; src/backup/merge.py; src/database/read_snapshot.py; src/database/pool_watch.py; src/static/app-core.js; src/static/taskmanager.js; tests/storage_guard_node_test.js
summary: A handle_error observer on the corpus engine, every lane engine and the read-snapshot engine reads the driver's SQLITE_CORRUPT code (never a wrong-key 26, never a missing-function, module or collation schema message (a schema row that names a missing table or column is damage), never a bound value that says malformed) and latches that file: the corpus latch stops collection admission, maintenance and the housekeeping lanes, a Wikipedia latch stops that lane's writing (the loop and, within a window, its tiers), a law latch skips the law step, any other file's incident is recorded and named only. One incident record per (file, scope, statement shape) per process in data/database-damage.json (newest 20, repeats counted, no value, no passphrase, a route template and never a raw path) under storage_guard.state(detail=True)['database_damage']. A statement over the full-text index that does not also read the articles table files the incident as the index, as a suspicion with its basis (a damaged index reads as plain 11 through MATCH; the gated Search statement reads both and is data), and the worst scope wins. The latch is released by the operator starting collection, running it now, going online or the unattended start (the corpus's and the law file's; going online also starts the Wikipedia lane, whose own start releases its file) or by a swapped-in corpus file, never by itself and never by a courtesy resume after a backup or a restore; 'Resume anyway' is refused while the corpus is latched; the failing statement waits at most 2 s for its record, on one record thread per job. The notice is drawn in the task manager and the vitals panel in 12 languages and says nothing is repaired and that the app has deleted nothing because of it. Verify, repair and salvage are E2 and E3; the layer-2 items not built (Home line, read-route sentence, checkpoints, background writers, backup window) are in OPEN_QUEUE.md. Each claim has a test, and the main ones were run against a mutant of their code.
